**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement meets the playbook's **preferred** position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer):

- **§1 (Kubient Services, p0001)** affirmatively disclaims exclusivity: "Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient," and confirms the agreement "will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties." This is language that benefits AP, so it stays as drafted.
- A full-text sweep for "exclusive", "sole", and third-party restriction phrasing turned up no all-requirements, sole-provider, or non-procurement covenant binding AP. The remaining hits are benign: a non-exclusive license granted **to** AP (p0002), exclusive jurisdiction in New York (p0064), each party's ownership of its own marks (p0065), and the standard no-third-party-beneficiary clause (p0073).

No fallback mechanics (category/12-month limit, performance-based exit) are needed, since there is no exclusivity to narrow.
